jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Field Testing
jokes.joke: I invented a lie detector and tested it at a used-car dealership. The salesman said, “This beauty was owned by one careful elderly lady.” My machine didn’t beep—it just printed a resignation letter and rolled itself into traffic.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: The Odometer Whisperer
jokes.joke: My uncle's an inventor. Not the cool kind. He invented a device that rolls back odometers, and he sells his cars himself, so he's basically an inventor, a manufacturer, and a con man all in one guy, which really cuts down on his supply chain. Thanksgiving, he showed me his newest patent. I said, “Uncle Ray, that's just a screwdriver.” He said, “Not the way I use it.”

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Goth Retriever
jokes.joke: My high school goth phase was a total disaster. You can't successfully project a black and dark aura when you have the completely uninhibited personality of a golden retriever. I’d be stomping around the mall in a heavy trench coat and combat boots, just aggressively waving at people like, “Hey! Life is a bottomless abyss, but these Auntie Anne's pretzel bites are amazing!”

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Lot of Regret
jokes.joke: So I roll into this used car dealership last Saturday, cash in hand, ready for freedom. Salesman swears this sedan is a gem, barely driven by a grandma. I buy it, cruise off the lot blasting music like I'm in a commercial. Two miles later the brakes fail and I'm fishtailing into a ditch. An unexpected change of plans: what I thought was my upgrade turned into an expensive paperweight and a long walk home. Next time I'm just sticking with the bus and my dignity.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Midnight Test Drive
jokes.joke: I once bought a car from this used‑lot inventor who was way too proud of his “custom features.” I turn the key and the headlights flicker like a haunted porch. He goes, “That’s intentional—mood lighting for night driving.” I hit the brakes and the horn plays a sad trombone. I’m like, “Man, I don’t need a vehicle with feelings. I just need it to stop before I do.”
